purpose: Phase-6C population-intervention policy. Phase-6C interventions are the POPULATION ECHO of the Phase-6B single-cell interventions: they act on the upstream single-cell apoptosis trajectory that the Population Engine reads read-only, so the population composition already reflects them. Phase 6C Part 1 defines NO population-only intervention (no double-counting); the descriptors below document the inherited, upstream-applied consequences only.

policy.explanation: A Phase-6B intervention (e.g. ROS scavenger, PI3K activator, caspase inhibitor, AIF knockdown) reshapes the single (modal) cell's commitment/execution. Because the Population Engine derives its fractions from that trajectory, the population response follows automatically - the intervention is not re-applied at the population layer.

mouse_b16bl6_population.population_consequence: fewer cells reach commitment -> apoptotic_fraction accumulates less
committed cells still accumulate (AIF branch) -> apoptotic_fraction largely unchanged
dominant branch attenuated -> execution drive lower, apoptotic accumulation slower; commitment unchanged

mouse_b16f10_population.population_consequence: survival restored before the gate -> population stays viable (little apoptotic accumulation)
